svg.text: Sliding-window attention: the window, the ring and the prefill index
One sequence · default settings (5 draft tokens) · window 128 is the value in the docs, not in the repo
window W = 128 ring = W + 6 = 134 slots one slot = 528 B (FP8 + scales) per layer, per sequence
Which keys does one decode query read?
The last 128 positions from the ring, plus compressed entries from the whole history.
window
▼ query
Query at position 1000 reads positions 873..1000 (128 keys, itself included) from the window.
A compressed layer also reads compressed entries (dots: an example top-k choice of a sparse layer).
Where does the window live? In a ring of 134 slots
Decode step at positions 1000..1005 (1 token + 5 drafts). slot = state_id × 134 + position % 134.
ring slots 0..66
ring slots 67..133
Blue: window of the query at 1000 = positions 873..1000 (slots 69..133, then 0..62, the ring wraps).
Pink: drafts 1001..1005 in slots 63..67. Grey: slot 68 still holds position 872, which no query of this step needs.
Example: state_id 3, position 1000 → 3 × 134 + 62 = slot 464 of swa_cache. (prepare_tensor_input_v4.cpp:104)
Prefill: how does a query find its window?
One sequence: 2,048 cached tokens, 300 new tokens. Keys come from two sections of one gathered buffer.
buffer
section 1: history 1920..2047
section 2: new tokens 2048..2347 (this chunk)
query 2048
127 history keys + 1 new key (itself)
query 2248
0 history keys + 128 new keys (2121..2248)
C++ writes 4 numbers per query (pivots: start and length in each section). The TileLang kernel
expand_swa_index turns them into int32 [T, 128] key indices, with −1 for unused columns.
Legend
window keys
query token
draft tokens
history / compressed
not needed
Simplified: one layer and one sequence. Every layer has its own ring in the sequence's state slot; the ring is 134 slots
only with the defaults (DEEPINFER_PREFILL_STORE_EXTRA_STATE off, DEEPINFER_USE_NEXTN_DECODE = 5).
